questions.question: How did you design the MCP-Based Business Agents and Real-Time Voice Agent at WorksBuddy?
questions.sampleAnswer: For WorksBuddy, I developed MCP-based AI agents (Lio, Taro, Evox & Inzo) for lead, task, email, and invoice management, integrating business APIs with context-aware execution and robust error handling. In parallel, I architected a multilingual real-time voice agent using LangGraph, Pipecat, LiveKit, Deepgram STT, and ElevenLabs TTS with Mem0 memory integration, achieving 1-2 second end-to-end response latency across APIs and telephony.

questions.question: What role does agentic orchestration play in your Retrieval-Augmented Q&A System (RAG)?
questions.sampleAnswer: We integrated a LangGraph supervisor agent over our LangChain RAG pipeline. When a similarity query is run in FAISS, the supervisor checks the retrieval confidence. If the retrieved context is insufficient or ambiguous, it triggers a dynamic CrewAI re-querying agent to expand terms and resolve vocabulary mismatches, boosting query resolution to 97%.

questions.question: How did you implement the Document Intelligence OCR pipeline with local LLMs?
questions.sampleAnswer: We built a privacy-focused REST API using FastAPI, PaddleOCR, and local Ollama LLMs (Phi-3 / Llama 3.2). PaddleOCR performs character and layout extraction from invoices, resumes, and visiting cards, which is structured by the local LLM and strictly validated using Pydantic schemas, reducing manual data-entry by ~70% without external API costs.

questions.question: How did you identify key academic outcome drivers during your internship at JSPIDERS?
questions.sampleAnswer: At JSPIDERS, I conducted exploratory data analysis (EDA) on student performance datasets using Python, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn. By segmenting data across parental education, test preparation, gender, and lunch type, I quantified relationships associated with up to 20% variance in scores, delivering data-driven recommendations for academic improvement.

questions.question: How did you design the Autonomous AI Leads & People Enrichment Platform for high concurrency?
questions.sampleAnswer: I engineered the platform using FastAPI, Next.js, and Redis Streams with concurrent workers to process 5,000-10,000+ professional profiles. It performs Google SERP profile discovery without LinkedIn auth, verifies emails via DNS MX/SPF/DMARC and SMTP handshake checks, and runs Groq LLMs (Llama/Qwen) for executive summaries and prospect-quality scoring with defensive database upserts.
